newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria demands data on dump-sites from oil firms.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria demands data on dump-sites from oil firms.

text.p: Environmental watchdog, the Federal Environment Protection Agency (FEPA) has asked all oil companies operating in Nigeria to submit a list and information on their dump-sites, local newspapers reported on Thursday.

Adegoke Adegoroye, FEPA's acting chief executive, told a seminar on environment in Lagos on Wednesday that this was necessary because of increasing complaints of pollution from oil-producing communities and environmental campaigners.
Dump-sites are where the wastes of multinationals flow into during and after oil mining activities.

"After receiving the inventory from the companies, we shall commission studies to determine the level of pollution in each operation area as a basis for remediation and calculation of compensation and liability," Adegoroye said.
Pollution is a sensitive issue in Nigeria where oil-producing communities demand compensation from multinationals whom they accuse of causing damage to the ecology through their mining activities.
The companies agree their operations cause some damage but in turn accuse the communities of sabotage and vandalising their equipment.
Adegoroye said for each dump-site, information like history, description, site, the geology and ecology and photographs were required.
